discovery: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene: prediction and discovery of flat-band correlated insulating and superconducting states in moire materials

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics / nanoscale and 2D materials
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic' angle near 1.1 degrees would flatten the electronic bands, so that electron-electron interactions would dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group built such devices with precise twist control. They found correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity, and both results have since been reproduced many times in laboratories worldwide. The work created a new field, twistronics. In it, a purely mechanical degree of freedom, the twist angle between atomic layers, tunes a material through Mott-like insulators, superconductors, orbital magnets and, in related moire systems, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states. It changed what we think can be engineered at the nanoscale. Strongly correlated quantum matter can now be designed, gated and measured in a single clean device, rather than having to be found in complex crystals. This is a rare and robust case of theory predicting a discovery that opened a whole field.
